bugs.root_cause: login_log.user_id is a FK to users(id) with no ON DELETE CASCADE (table has no migration file — created directly in Supabase dashboard, drifted from repo schema). Any user who ever logged in has login_log rows, so a raw `supabase.from('users').delete()` throws a Postgres FK violation (23503), swallowed into a generic 500. The same delete call exists in merge/route.ts's second step, so a merge would move roles to keep_id successfully then fail to delete delete_id, leaving a roleless ghost account that read to the admin as 'role duplication'.
bugs.fix: In both routes, run `supabase.from('login_log').update({ user_id: null }).eq('user_id', <id>)` before the users delete (login_log already stores full_name/phone independently, so this is safe — see login-report and analytics routes which fall back to full_name). Also added explicit handling for Postgres error code 23503 to return a clearer 409 instead of a generic 500. Added supabase/migrations/20260702_fix_login_log_user_fk.sql to fix the FK at the DB level (ON DELETE SET NULL) — NOT YET APPLIED to the live DB (no DB credentials in this session); user must run it via Supabase SQL editor or `supabase db push`.
